instrument.state: An ordered sequence of revisions contains a transition in a reproducibly testable property, with at least one earlier state known not to have the property and one later state known to have it.
instrument.operation: Test an intermediate revision, use the result to discard the incompatible portion of the remaining history, and repeat the partition-and-test process until the transition is localized.
instrument.signal: Each tested revision is classified on one side or the other of the target property, progressively shrinking the interval that can contain the transition.
instrument.inference: Repeated elimination constrains the first revision associated with the observed change to the final unresolved boundary or commit.
instrument.limit: Flaky tests, unbuildable revisions, nonmonotonic behavior, multiple independent changes, interactions among revisions, or an incorrectly chosen good or bad endpoint can prevent unique localization or identify a boundary that is correlated with rather than solely causal of the behavior.

target.question: Which parts of the proposed onboarding redesign are necessary for users to complete activation, and what interactions prevent a simple feature ranking?
evidence: Authored synthetic scenario; no claim about a real organization or person.

An ordered synthetic prototype history has a known successful earlier revision and failing later revision under the same deterministic recorded activation replay. Every intermediate revision is executable. Independent exhaustive prior characterization establishes a single transition for this fixed replay, not a population claim.

Revision manifests identify the changed interaction rules at the boundary; a boundary may contain several interacting changes. The study seeks a bounded contribution to the broader parts-and-interactions question.

mapping.state: An ordered onboarding revision history brackets one reproducible activation-failure transition.
mapping.operation: Test intermediate revisions on the fixed activation replay, discard the incompatible half of the remaining history, and repeat until the transition is localized; inspect the boundary manifest without assigning independent feature effects.
mapping.signal: Success or failure at each tested revision shrinks the interval containing the activation transition.
mapping.inference: Localize the first revision associated with failure and the proposal parts changed there, selecting a bounded interaction cluster for further necessity testing rather than claiming that each changed part is independently necessary.
mapping.limit: Flakiness, unexecutable revisions, nonmonotonicity and incorrect endpoints would invalidate localization; even a unique boundary can contain interacting changes and establishes association rather than a unique cause or general user necessity.
